title: Write on notes filtered only by id from the request
description: The record is chosen by id, which the caller controls, and the query has no filter on the signed-in user. Changing the id in the request reaches other users' records. If row level security already restricts this table to the owner and the query runs with the user's own client, this is defense in depth; with a service-role or admin client it is the only check. saas-audit rates this high; that is its own static rating, not a demonstrated impact. Suggested change: Add an ownership condition taken from the session (for example .eq("user_id", user.id) or where: { id, userId: session.user.id }) and treat zero matched rows as 404.
claimed_root_cause: A record is chosen by an id from the request with no ownership filter, or a row owner is set from client input.

title: Webhook does not deduplicate events
description: Stripe delivers events at least once and retries on any non-2xx answer, so the same event can arrive twice. title: Request body is parsed before the signature is verified
description: The signature covers the exact bytes Stripe sent. Parsing the body first and re-serialising it changes those bytes, so verification fails in production. The usual workaround, trusting the parsed body and dropping verification, removes the protection altogether. saas-audit rates this high; that is its own static rating, not a demonstrated impact. Suggested change: Use "const rawBody = await request.text()" and pass rawBody to constructEvent; parse JSON only from the verified event.
claimed_root_cause: A Stripe webhook handler parses or re-serialises the body before verifying the signature, which either breaks verification or means the verified bytes are not the ones used.

title: Unhandled event types make the handler fail (returns 500)
description: Stripe sends every event type the endpoint is subscribed to. A non-2xx answer for an event you simply do not handle is retried for days and, after repeated failures, the endpoint is disabled, which then also drops the events you do care about. saas-audit rates this low; that is its own static rating, not a demonstrated impact. Suggested change: Return 200 for unhandled types (log them) and reserve error statuses for events you tried to process and failed. Subscribe the endpoint only to the events you handle.

title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML receives non-constant input
description: Anything that reaches this sink is parsed as HTML in the visitor's browser. If any part of it comes from a user, a database row or a third-party API, that is stored or reflected cross-site scripting, and an XSS bug can read the session and call every API as the user. saas-audit rates this high; that is its own static rating, not a demonstrated impact. Suggested change: Render the value as text (JSX escapes it).
